MomentumScore-Style Review — Exit Rank 52

Report 48's strategy skeleton (Midcap150 momentum 10, NIFTY-50 200-EMA regime filter, GOLDBEES hedge) re-run with MomentumScore's review layer on top: a held stock is sold only when it falls below rank 52 of the eligible universe, carried names keep their original shares, reviews happen at scheduled month-ends (Jun/Dec) plus every regime flip, and every leg pays 0.1%/side. The run ships with a real-rupee trade log, an Indian capital-gains tax estimate, the 10-target health scorecard, both-halves and date-luck robustness checks, and a live ranking preview.

2009-01-02–2026-10-16
Report generated 2026-10-16 21:36
● After costs: CAGR +39.5% at -25.4% max drawdown — NIFTY 50 made +12.1% ● After the tax estimate: +34.4% a year ▲ Health score 60/100 — both-halves PASS, date-luck PASS

The review layer does not change the regime filter — it changes which stocks are held and when they are sold. That means the whipsaw is inherited intact: this run logs 65 regime exits and 64 re-entries across 2009-01-02–2026-10-16, the same behaviour report 48 showed with its 69 re-entries. Costs and the tax estimate are what move the headline numbers: +41.7% before costs, +39.5% after 0.1%/side on every leg, +34.4% after the capital-gains estimate — still roughly three times NIFTY 50's +12.1%, with a materially shallower drawdown than the index.

Limitations

▲ read before trusting any number above

WHAT THIS SHOWS — every simplification behind this backtest.

  • The whipsaw is inherited from report 48's regime filter, unchanged: 65 regime exits and 64 re-entries in this run (report 48 logged 69 re-entries). The review layer deliberately does not try to dampen it — it changes the stock-holding rules, not the market-timing rule.
  • Health: 9 of the 10 target ranges are MomentumScore's published ones; the "tail risk" checks (monthly and per-trade) use skewness as a documented proxy because MomentumScore's exact definition is not published. Curve checks here run on the engine's full-resolution daily curve; the webapp's cross-report lab scores archived chart series (≤1500 points), so a lab score can differ by a check.
  • Tax: FY-by-FY estimate on the trade log — exit-date-based FY assignment, 4% cess, no surcharge, no advance-tax timing, no pre-2018 grandfathering; the s.112A 31-Jan-2025 FMV map affected 0 trades here because every position was held under a year. Not tax advice.
  • Costs: a flat 0.1% per side on every leg including the gold hedge — no slippage or market-impact model, and no allowance for the fact that small-cap fills are usually worse than midcap ones.
  • Design choices in the review layer: carried stocks keep their original shares (report 31's convention, no re-equalisation); freed cash refills slots at the next review; a regime re-entry buys a fresh top-10 without hysteresis (the exit-rank rule only protects positions during an ongoing regime, not across one).
  • Same reconstruction caveats as report 48: today's fixed Midcap150 constituent list applied retroactively (survivorship bias), equal weighting, unadjusted prices, no dividends modeled, no F&O-eligibility screen.
  • Date luck: the mid-month variant (day ~15) is one alternative calendar, a smoke test — not the full six-calendar sweep of reports 85/92.
  • Rupee figures (P&L, tax) scale the window start to ₹1,00,000 through the engine's own unit accounting; the percentage curves are scale-free.
